story: On a sunny, 81-degree Saturday morning in Sumter Oaks, Gary and Donna have both set off for Magnolia Loop, where Hal is dutifully counting the pink flamingos on the lawns against his notebook tally. Back at her house, Rosa is content to scrub the baking trays and wipe down the counters before tonight's Halloween gathering. Gary is hopeful about the day, and Donna is in fine spirits as she makes her way down the street.
events: Gary headed to Magnolia Loop (the street).
Donna headed to Magnolia Loop (the street).
Hal (donna flamingo flock): Count the flamingos visible from the street and compare against my notebook tally
Rosa (rosa kitchen): Wash the baking trays and wipe down the counters so everything's tidy before tonight

gary.thought_process: I'm at home on a sunny Halloween morning, and everything for the cart is already bench-tested and sorted. The approval from Architectural Review (L-01) is still pending, so I can't mount anything visible from the street. The parade is at 6, so time matters. I've already checked in once at tick 228 and offered the sketches. The sensible move is to go back to the Architectural Review desk to see if the committee has signed off, bringing the sketches and clamp list, so I'm ready to mount the moment it's approved. Nobody's around to talk to, and nothing more to do on the bench.

parameters.content: Heading out to check on my Architectural Review application. Parade's at 6 and the cart's ready to go the second they sign off.

donna.thought_process: I already penciled in the calendar, checked my bag, and texted Gary to confirm one o'clock and the 6 PM parade. No one's around to talk to, and Gary hasn't answered yet, so there's no point nagging him again. The costume contest sign-up clipboard at Town Square is the one loose end, and it keeps me at the center of the Halloween scene. I'll head out to Magnolia Loop, see the pumpkins, and swing by the sign-up table before the court time.

parameters.content: Heading out to see the pumpkins on the Loop and put my name on the costume-contest clipboard before one o'clock.

hal.thought_process: I'm back on Magnolia Loop with my notebook counts in hand. The flock is right here, and the L-02 limit is three visible ornaments, so I want an exact tally before I file anything with the committee. Fair is fair: count first, report second. Parade is tomorrow evening and I'd like the record straight before then.

parameters.content: Count the flamingos visible from the street and compare against my notebook tally

rosa.thought_process: The treats are baked, bagged, and stacked by the door, and Saturday evening is confirmed clear. Nobody is nearby, and the trick-or-treaters don't come until tonight. The kitchen is the one place where I still have something to tidy: the trays and counters need cleaning before the evening rush. I'll clear the kitchen so everything is ready and I can head out to the Loop later to see Gary and Donna without scrambling.

parameters.content: Wash the baking trays and wipe down the counters so everything's tidy before tonight

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
